about: Every CPG variable sorted into input / optimisation / fixed / dependent. 'cad_variables' are the 119 variables CPG writes to CADs/CPG/cpg_equations_onshape.txt, in that order; 'code_only' are values the code uses but does not write to the CAD file (including the small module module_s: the CAD file has one module); 'unused_config_blocks' are config blocks CPG never reads. tests/test_variable_categories.py checks the lists against the code and re-evaluates every formula and lookup; docs/variables/cpg.md is generated from this file (python tools/variables/render.py).

categories.input: chosen parts and material: the motor's dimensions and torque, the motor driver's mount dimensions, the gear material's allowable stress
categories.optimisation: searched by the optimiser: teeth, module, number of planets
categories.fixed: constants that don't depend on the design: clearances, wall thicknesses, fastener and bearing choices, feature sizes, the gear standard
categories.dependent: computed from the variables above, by a formula, a catalogue lookup (bearings, bolts, nuts) or a rule the code applies (the tooth-stress rule for face widths)

confidence.high: the code reads it directly from one source, or computes it with an explicit formula
confidence.medium: the code is clear, but the category is a judgement call (see the reason)
confidence.low: can't be decided from the code alone

cad_variables.name: Nr

cad_variables.name: fw_s_calc
cad_variables.rule: two stress widths, b = FOS x Ft x qe x qk / (gear_allowable_stress x module): b1 for the sun - big planet mesh (module, Ft from serviceFactor x motor_peak_torque at the sun, qe from the sun-planet contact ratio, qk from Ns) and b2 for the small planet - ring mesh (module_s, qk from Np_s); then, if b1 + b2 < 2 x planet_bearing_width + standard_clearance_1_5mm x 2/3, each planet is raised to at least planet_bearing_width + standard_clearance_1_5mm x 1/3 (mitStressAnalysisMinFacewidth); fw_s_calc = b1
cad_variables.reason: sun face width from the tooth-stress rule of the sun - big planet mesh (b1): fixed by the optimisation variables, the motor torque, the gear material and the safety factors. The printed sun uses fw_s_used

cad_variables.name: fw_r
cad_variables.rule: two stress widths, b = FOS x Ft x qe x qk / (gear_allowable_stress x module): b1 for the sun - big planet mesh (module, Ft from serviceFactor x motor_peak_torque at the sun, qe from the sun-planet contact ratio, qk from Ns) and b2 for the small planet - ring mesh (module_s, qk from Np_s); then, if b1 + b2 < 2 x planet_bearing_width + standard_clearance_1_5mm x 2/3, each planet is raised to at least planet_bearing_width + standard_clearance_1_5mm x 1/3 (mitStressAnalysisMinFacewidth); fw_r = b2 (raised)

cad_variables.name: bearing_mount_thickness
cad_variables.formula: output_mounting_hole_dia * 2 if bearing_OD + output_mounting_hole_dia * 4 > Nr * module_s + 2 * h_b_s else ((Nr * module_s + 2 * h_b_s) - (bearing_OD + output_mounting_hole_dia * 4)) / 2 + output_mounting_hole_dia * 2 + standard_clearance_1_5mm
cad_variables.reason: two-case rule: a wall of two bolt diameters when the bearing is wider than the ring gear, otherwise wide enough to cover the ring teeth; the factors 2 and 4 are hard-coded (also in the mass code; SSPG uses bearing_mount_wall_bolt_dia_multiple)

cad_variables.reason: ring gear wall: 5 mm, or thicker so the ring reaches the output bearing; the 5 is hard-coded twice and the mass model always uses ringRadialWidthMM (ISSUES bug 17). In SSPG it is a fixed config value

cad_variables.name: fw_p_b
cad_variables.rule: two stress widths, b = FOS x Ft x qe x qk / (gear_allowable_stress x module): b1 for the sun - big planet mesh (module, Ft from serviceFactor x motor_peak_torque at the sun, qe from the sun-planet contact ratio, qk from Ns) and b2 for the small planet - ring mesh (module_s, qk from Np_s); then, if b1 + b2 < 2 x planet_bearing_width + standard_clearance_1_5mm x 2/3, each planet is raised to at least planet_bearing_width + standard_clearance_1_5mm x 1/3 (mitStressAnalysisMinFacewidth); fw_p_b = b1 (raised)
cad_variables.reason: big-planet width from the tooth-stress rule (b1, raised to the planet-bearing minimum when the two planets together are too short for their bearings); the planet-bearing minimum has hard-coded factors 2/3 and 1/3 of standard_clearance_1_5mm (SSPG uses planet_bearing_gap)

code_only.name: motor_peak_torque
code_only.reason: motor torque the gears are sized for (peak torque under the default rating setting); sets the face widths

code_only.name: gear_allowable_stress
code_only.reason: allowable tooth stress of the gear material, chosen with the material mode (3dp: PLA, metal: steel); sets the face widths

code_only.name: FOS
code_only.reason: factor of safety in the tooth-stress rule

code_only.name: serviceFactor
code_only.reason: service factor on the motor torque in the tooth-stress rule

code_only.name: clearance_motor_and_case_min
code_only.reason: smallest radial gap between the motor and the case; sets clearance_motor_and_case (CAD) and the case mass

code_only.name: output_mounting_hole_num
code_only.reason: number of output mounting holes: read from the config but not used by the code or written to the CAD file

code_only.name: module_s
code_only.reason: the small module (small planet, ring): searched by the optimiser loop, but not in the CAD file (which has one module; ISSUES bug 18)

code_only.name: h_b_s
code_only.reason: ring tooth depth (small module), used by the bearing-mount rule

code_only.name: maxGearboxDiameter
code_only.formula: (MAX_GB_DIA_MULT_FACTOR_SMALL_MOTOR if motor_OD < SMALL_MOTOR_DIA_MM else MAX_GB_DIA_MULT_FACTOR) * motor_OD
code_only.reason: largest gearbox diameter the optimiser may use (gearbox_runner max_diameter; unlike SSPG, without subtracting the ring wall)

code_only.name: actuator_width
code_only.formula: fw_r + clearance_planet + bearing_height + clearance_planet + case_dist + bearing_retainer_thickness + motor_height + case_mounting_surface_height + standard_clearance_1_5mm + base_plate_thickness
code_only.reason: axial width without the driver mount, written to the results CSV
